subject: Discovery recap — PayNex TCO constraints & batching options
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@paynex.com>, Asha Verma <asha.verma@paynex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap — PayNex TCO constraints & batching options

Hi Liam / Asha,

Thanks for the time today — appreciated the clear explanation of PayNex's constraints. Quick recap so we have alignment and can move to a tight pilot scope: 

Key pain points you called out:
- Monthly token spend is the gating concern; current procurement ceiling is ~$40k/mo for the inference stack.
- SLOs: 95th percentile latency target is ~200 ms for core payment flows; some batch-y endpoints can accept higher tail.
- Burst patterns: weekday peak between 14:00–17:00 PST with short, high-concurrency bursts (1000–1500 req/min).
- Quality: must preserve current model correctness for fraud scoring and decisioning; occasional fallbacks okay if flagged.

Workload assumptions we discussed (please flag if any differ):
- Typical request: 350 tokens in + 75 tokens out on average (longer in edge cases).
- Expected steady state: ~3M requests / month, peak concurrency as above.
- Primary route is low-latency scoring; non-real-time enrichment flows can tolerate batching to reduce cost.

Suggested levers and initial TCO framing (high level):
1) Batching + autoscale pools for enrichment endpoints — estimate 30–45% reduction on token cost for those routes.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated user contexts (sessions) on scoring flow — 10–20% token reduction observed on similar customers.
3) Model quantization variant for fallback offline scoring (lower cost but slightly higher latency) — useful for background recomputations.
4) Smart routing: route non-critical traffic to a cheaper model variant in bursts to avoid breaching the monthly spend cap.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a short TCO worksheet for you to drop in actual QPS/tokens so we can produce a 3-month spend projection (attached).
- If you’re comfortable, please share a 48–72 hour sample of production QPS/median token lengths — we can run a quick costing run and batching sensitivity.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review the model-level cost/savings map and define pilot success metrics.

If the high-level numbers look right, I can sketch a pilot that keeps your critical SLOs intact while targeting a 25–40% decrease in month-1 unit cost.

Thanks and happy to adjust if I misunderstood anything.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: PayNex-TCO-worksheet.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB), redwood_batching_onepager.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@paynex.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Verma <asha.verma@paynex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PayNex TCO constraints & batching options

Jonas — thanks for the clean recap. Couple of clarifications / asks from our side: 

- The $40k/mo cap is firm for Q3 — we can re-evaluate afterwards but pilot must fit within that envelope (or show a clear path).
- We can share a 72-hour sample early next week (will scrub PII). Expect ~120k requests/day over the sample window.
- Our engineering team cares about p95 latency on the scoring endpoint; if batching introduces any risk to hitting p95 <200ms we need a fallback.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you include a conservative downside scenario in the worksheet (assume no caching + minimal batching) so we can see the delta?
2) Can you call out what the operational effort looks like for Private vs. Hosted modes (we likely prefer hosted initially but want to understand isolation options)?

Asha and I are available Tue/Thu afternoons next week for the follow-up.

—Liam
Liam O'Neill
Head of Engineering | PayNex
liam.oneill@paynex.com | (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 12:07:00 +0000

Jonas / Karthik — forwarding Liam's clarification. Two operational notes before we finalize the worksheet: 

- For hosted mode, we should prepare a short appendix that lists: encryption at rest/in transit, optional VPC peering for network isolation, and SLA options for Dedicated (if they ask later).
- For the conservative downside scenario, let's use: no KV cache, 0% batching for scoring routes, 50% of enrichment flows batched. That will stress the spend side.

I'll help draft the hosted vs private ops bullets — Jonas, if you can add the baseline cost numbers in the sheet with columns for: baseline, moderate batching, aggressive caching + batching, that will make the decision read clearer.

Marissa
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@paynex.com>, Asha Verma <asha.verma@paynex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PayNex TCO constraints & batching options

Liam / Asha — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the sample window. Attached is the worksheet you can drop numbers into; I added three scenarios (Conservative / Baseline / Optimized) with callouts for which levers are active in each. Quick highlights in the worksheet: 

- Conservative: no KV cache, no batching on scoring, baseline model variant — estimate: ~$53k/mo (over your $40k cap) — included so we can show downside.
- Baseline: modest caching (10%) + 20% batching on enrichment flows — estimate: ~$38k/mo (within cap).
- Optimized: prefix caching + 40% batching + routing cheaper model for non-critical flows — estimate: ~$26k/mo.

Operational trade-offs:
- Hosted: fastest to pilot; supports token-level telemetry and quick rollouts. Can provide VPC peering and customer-managed keys for isolation; no on-prem hardware required.
- Private (VPC/On-prem): full isolation and control, higher setup time (~4–8 weeks) and onboarding cost; better for long-term compliance needs.

Pilot proposal (narrow):
1) 2-week technical validation using your 72-hour sample (we run costing + latency profiles) — no infra changes on your side.
2) 4-week pilot on hosted with canary routes for scoring (traffic-split 80:20) to validate p95 and cost delta.
3) Success criteria: scoring p95 <200ms and month-1 unit cost reduction >=25%.

Would Tue 14:00–14:30 or Thu 15:00–15:30 ET next week work for a walkthrough of the worksheet and to lock the pilot dates?

Thanks — attaching worksheet and the batching one-pager again.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
